statement: For a graph G, some common coupling K>0 and some frequencies produce an equilibrium with identically zero Jacobian if and only if G is bipartite. Set the phases on its two parts to 0 and pi/2 and define the frequencies by the equilibrium equations.

answer.text: Bipartiteness characterizes existence of completely degenerate equilibria in the common-positive-coupling subfamily.
answer.display: Bipartiteness characterizes existence of completely degenerate equilibria in the common-positive-coupling subfamily.

source.location: Theorem 10 and its proof, p. 6; equations (7)–(9)

notes:
Only the common positive edge-coupling subfamily is classified. This is a classification of a particular singularity type, not the entire discriminant or all singular equilibria. Migration: Merge exceptional-fibre behaviour into Exceptional locus; preserve each source result separately.
